question:
A 90-year-old male with alcoholic liver disease presents with sudden onset joint pain affecting his right
knee and left wrist. His medical history reveals untreated community-acquired pneumonia that began
one week ago following a camping trip to Connecticut. Initial symptoms included green sputum
production and pleuritic chest pain, with chest imaging showing right lower lobe consolidation. His
condition has deteriorated since then, despite being current with Covid-19 vaccinations and testing
negative for SARS-CoV-2. Physical examination reveals a temperature of 38.2°C, a new loud
holosystolic murmur radiating to the axilla, and right base dullness with egophony. Both affected joints
exhibit heat, swelling, and tenderness with severely restricted passive range of motion. Which
pathogen is most likely responsible for this patient's clinical presentation? Answer Choices: (A) Listeria
monocytogenes (B) Enterococcus faecalis (C) Streptococcus pyogenes (D) Neisseria gonorrhoeae (E)
Pseudomonas aeruginosa (F) Escherichia coli (G) Haemophilus influenzae (H) Borrelia burgdorferi (I)
Streptococcus pneumoniae (J) Staphylococcus aureus
 A. Haemophilus influenzae
B. Pseudomonas aeruginosa
C. Escherichia coli
D. Streptococcus pyogenes
E. Listeria monocytogenes
F. Staphylococcus aureus
G. Neisseria gonorrhoeae
H. Borrelia burgdorferi
I. Streptococcus pneumoniae

J. Enterococcus faecalis
